basicMistakes.where: Both team logo positions at the left and right ends of the top row. With the brief's own values they are empty discs, a dark ring on the left and a plain cream disc on the right, with no logo in either. The same empty discs appear in G-3, G-4 and in every operator-step frame.

otherProblems: Logos only show with the long values (G-5 to G-7), and even then each sits on a round plate of its own: a white shield on a dark disc and a navy shield on a cream disc. Neither is the real pale-yellow or burgundy mark set straight on the glass.
The info row says 'KARTTA 1 · MAP 3 · ANCIENT' (G-5). It gives two different map numbers and mixes Finnish and English, so a viewer cannot tell which map is being played.
In the long frames the right team name sits on one line but is set high (G-5, G-14). It is not centred on its logo or on the scores.

Long names drop to a much smaller size than short names (G-11, G-14). The two sides then carry very different visual weight: a tiny two-line name on one side against a large single-line name on the other.
Map final and Next map from the pre-match state show no visible change (G-29 to G-40). Only Map final after Go live shows PÄÄTTYNYT, and no frame shows the next map actually moving on.
answer.reasons: I would not put this on air as delivered. The layout itself is solid: a centred dark glass bar with yellow and burgundy accents, clear scores, and a readable Finnish phase badge that works for live, pause and final. All the operator actions the brief asks for are on the surface. The problem is that with the brief's own values the two logo spots are empty discs. A scorebug that has to carry both team logos goes out with two hollow circles, and when the logos do show they sit on round plates of their own. The info row also contradicts itself ('KARTTA 1 · MAP 3'), and long names leave the two sides unbalanced and slightly out of line. None of this is hard to fix, but it is not ready today.

otherProblems: With empty values (G-8, G-9, G-10) the panel stays full size and shows only 'DONATION' and the heart avatar in its top-left, so the plate reads largely empty. That is an edge case: real alerts always carry a name and an amount.
Hold gives no on-screen sign that the alert is held. The countdown rule at the bottom right is so faint it barely registers, which matters little to viewers but gives the operator nothing to watch.

The sample frames show a green heart placeholder in the avatar frame instead of a real avatar. The white avatar is only seen in the long-value frames (G-5 to G-7), where it sits cleanly on the dark green tile.
answer.reasons: This is a tidy dark alert card at the top right. It has a green accent bar, an avatar tile, a spaced 'DONATION' label with a green amount, a bold white name and a grey message. All the text reads well over the dark, light and busy grounds. The long umlaut name 'xX_Ängström_Gänseblümchen_Xx' fits on one line without clipping. The long message wraps to two clean lines that stay inside the panel and clear the thin countdown rule. The white shield avatar shows up well on its dark green tile. The animations are clean fades with no overlapping text. Skip clears the alert, Replay and Resume rebuild it correctly, and all four actions the brief needs (skip, replay, hold, resume) are on the operator surface. The only weakness is the mostly empty plate when values are empty, which a viewer would hardly ever see. As delivered it would go on air.

otherProblems: After the reveal the kicker still says 'THE NOMINEES'. Only the gold-outlined row marks the winner; there is no 'Winner' label.
Suspense is subtle: the nominees dim a little and the board scales up slightly. It reads more like a soft dim than a beat that builds tension.

With the long values, the director name becomes the large mixed-case primary line and the film title drops to the small mono line. In the sample frames the film title is primary, so the row hierarchy is not consistent between datasets.
With the long category, the title shrinks to fit but the gold rule keeps its position, so the gap between title and rule grows a little.
answer.reasons: G airs. It is a centred black-and-gold board with a solid dark panel, so the text stays clear over the light, busy and video backgrounds. Category, kicker and four nominee rows are evenly spaced, and the long names and titles fit inside their rows without clipping. Both required actions are on the operator surface and work: suspense dims the field, and reveal puts the winner's row in a gold frame with gold text while the others fade back. That frame is drawn cleanly and does not touch the text. The Take and Out are clean, and the empty state shows a tidy title. The remaining problems are small polish points a viewer would barely notice: the kicker doesn't change to a winner label, the suspense state is soft, and the long values swap which line is primary.
